title: Switzerland – Electrical installation work – PWA-B2, B3 (Selektiv) Ausschreibung Elektro, BKP 232 Niederspannungsinstallationen
description: Die Infrastruktur des Flughafens Zürich unterliegt einem schrittweisen Erneuerungsprozess. In den letzten 15 Jahren sind verschiedene Teile der zentralen Flughafeninfrastruktur umfassend saniert und erweitert worden: Das Dock B wurde komplett umgebaut, der Terminal 2 totalsaniert und erweitert, und zwischen den Terminal 1 und 2 wurde das neue Sicherheitskontrollgebäude mit zentralisiertem Zugang in das Airside Center erstellt. Derzeit werden die zentrale Gepäcksortieranlage nördlich des Terminal 1 erweitert und das flughafenweite Gepäcksortiersystem abgelöst und erneuert. In einem nächsten Schritt müssen die in die Jahre gekommenen Teile der zentralen Flughafen- Infrastruktur ersetzt werden: Das Dock A wurde zusammen mit dem Tower 1985 in Betrieb genommen und blieb in seiner Struktur bis heute weitgehend unverändert. Bezüglich Funktionalität, Nachhaltigkeit und Qualität kann das Dock A die heutigen Anforderungen nicht mehr erfüllen. Aufgrund einer umfassenden Analyse wurde entschieden, das bestehende Dock A durch einen Neubau nördlich des heutigen Gebäudes zu ersetzen. Der Ersatzneubau für das Dock A, der neue Tower und das umfassend sanierte Vorfeld zum Dock A mit allen weiteren Anpassungen, Erweiterungen und Umbauten der zentralen Flughafeninfrastruktur sind die sichtbar wichtigsten baulichen Massnahmen der nächsten 15 bis 20 Jahre. Bei der etappenweisen Realisierung muss gewährleistet werden, dass der Betrieb normal weitergeführt werden kann und mit den neu erstellten Gebäuden die künftigen funktionalen Anforderungen erfüllt werden können. Das Projekt PWA «Perimeterfreilegung Wurzel A» beinhaltet die Umsetzung von Anpassungen an bestehenden Medien und Anlagen. Diese befinden sich im und auch ausserhalb des Abbruchsperimeters der Wurzel Dock A. Die Arbeiten sind für den Bauzustand des Rückbaus und für die weiteren Phasen des Ersatzneubau Dock A im Zeitraum von 2026-2033 zu realisieren. Im Abbruchperimeter der Dockwurzel A sind essenzielle Teile der Gebäudetechnik für die Versorgung des Kontroll-Towers, Dockwurzel A, Dock A, Airside Center und der Passkontrollhalle verortet.

At this time, questions concerning the composition and requirements for a future RFP will not be entertained. 2.0 SUBJECT: The DHA R&PI, J8 Financial Operations is obtaining information for a potential non-personal services contract to provide administrative and technical execution services, as well as technical expertise, for the Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) activities, to include CDM optimization, enhancement, and operations, to support the DHA Electronic Health Record (EHR), Military Health System (MHS) GENESIS, and its itemized billing solution, RevX. 3.0 BACKGROUND: The DHA J-8 recognizes the need to enhance its RCM processes to ensure the efficient and effective management of healthcare finances within the MHS. Using the MHS GENESIS EHR as a catalyst, J-8 seeks to address several critical challenges within its RCM framework: Revenue Leakage and Inefficiencies, Compliance and Regulatory Risks, Data Accuracy and Integration, Patient Experience, Resource Utilization, Financial Transparency, Clean Audit Capability, and Technology and Innovation. In response to these challenges, DHA J-8 aims to launch the RCM Initiative to transform its RCM processes. The goal is to enhance workload capture, financial performance, compliance, patient satisfaction, and resource utilization while ensuring transparency and embracing innovative technologies within the MHS. Industry practice is to document, and bill patient encounters based on an itemized list of charges. To ensure documented care in MHS GENESIS results in an all-inclusive itemized bill within RevX, numerous actions must occur throughout the revenue cycle process (assignment of Patient Identification Process (PIP), provider documentation, medical record coding, and patient billing). Administration staff must ensure the PIP providers completely document and select the proper patient orderable description of care provided. Medical record coders must properly code the care provided. Finally, Uniform Business Office (UBO) staff must properly generate a bill on established separate billing forms for professional charges and institutional charges. The DHA supports and provides medical care for the Department of War, 9.4 million eligible beneficiaries through the $52 billion Defense Health Program (DHP), which includes contracted healthcare networks and Military Treatment Facilities (MTFs). The deployment of MHS GENESIS is complete and currently in a transition phase. While this major technology transformation has provided a significant set of enhanced revenue cycle and business management capabilities for the MHS, they have also brought new requirements to align with industry-leading practices and underscored underlying issues in the legacy environment. For the Government to fully realize the benefits of MHS GENESIS revenue cycle capabilities, these cross-functional challenges require an integrated approach to resolve. The Government will direct the actual implementation and detailed tasks for the RCM Activity as the MHS lacks knowledgeable in-house staffing to execute these specific operations. Specific assistance is required to support the DHA Financial Operations, J-8 with capabilities for optimization of revenue cycle efforts to prioritize improvement opportunities, begin reducing work queue backlog in MHS GENESIS, increase clinical workload capture, increase total billed for Third Party Collections (TPC), identify and correct areas where revenue leakage may be occurring, improve enterprise knowledge of workload and revenue capture, and enhance MTF staffs' ability to manage their business and be audit-ready. 4.0 RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS: Respondents should address the following in their response: 4.1 Organization Information: a. title: License to Access the American Hospital Association Inc.�s (AHA) Proprietary Databases, Training, and Technical Support
description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention intends to award a sole source firm fixed price purchase order to American Hospital Association (AHA) for the Office of Public Health data, Surveillance, and Technology, OPHDST/IDD/ADB, to maintain and continue licenses to access AHA�s proprietary Annual Survey, AHA Healthcare IT, Payment, and Financial databases, and associated software, online tools, virtual training, and technical /consultative support. The American Hospital Association, Inc. (AHA) conducts multiple surveys with hospitals to include the Annual Survey, which is the main survey that profiles a universe of 6,200+ hospitals and 400 health care systems throughout the United States. Comprising over 1,300+ hospital data points gathered directly from the source, the AHA Annual Survey Database (ASDB) offers facility-level insights on different topics including organizational structure and affiliations; beds and utilization; staffing with physicians included; expenses; accreditations and approval codes; and telehealth and remote patient monitoring. AHA also provides a Healthcare IT Database which provides information on several healthcare IT indicators that illustrate the depth and level of technology integration within hospitals. The database contains hospital level information on over 2,600 hospitals. This IT survey is the most reliable source of hospital IT implementation information available and is used as a foundation for national research and government studies, including national EHR adoption rates. In addition to these surveys, AHA also provides financial module data, a third-party database developed by AHA largely as a service/support element for clients of the AHA ASDB. AHA�s survey data is the only available data source solely focused on hospital and health system characteristics. This contract action is for services for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of FAR 13.106-1(b) (SAP). All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotations; however, all quotations /responses received within 15 days of the issuance of this notice shall be considered by the government. A determination by the government not to compete this proposed contract, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the government. title: Medium Unmanned Surface Vessel (MUSV) Phase II Integration and Testing
description: The Department of the Navy Direct Reporting Portfolio Manager (DRPM) / Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) for Robotics and Autonomous Systems (RAS) hereby issues this announcement regarding a forthcoming Area of Interest (AOI) for Medium Unmanned Surface Vehicles (MUSV) Phase II Integration and Testing. MUSV uses modular design principles to create adaptable and resilient solutions that can effectively counter evolving threats. We invite interested parties with expertise in innovative solutions to complex problems, vessel construction, autonomy, perception systems, and general maritime experience to participate in this opportunity. Vendors will be evaluated on platform maturity, open-architecture autonomy compatibility, endurance, payload integration capacity, and rapid-production scalability. To meet the critical operational demand signal for high-volume autonomous vessel procurement over the next decade, DRPM RAS will employ innovative and streamlined acquisition pathways. The government will leverage the authorities of 10 U.S.C. 3458 (Commercial Solutions) and 10 U.S.C. 4022 (Other Transactions) and intends to award Basic Ordering Agreements and prototype other transaction agreements, and potentially production contracts or transactions to successful vendors. To maintain technical superiority and capture rapid commercial innovations, DRPM RAS intends to issue the AOI with a rolling open window. This open call will allow new entrants to compete and existing vendors to submit updated product blocks and modular payload configurations. Approved platforms will be accepted into the maritime marketplace hosted on drones.mil. This digital clearinghouse will empower authorized acquisition authorities and operational stakeholders across the Department of War enterprise to rapidly configure and issue funded delivery orders for vetted maritime autonomous systems without redundant procurement cycles. Formal AOI release is planned on or before September 30, 2026. Detailed AOI instructions will be released via SAM.gov and syndicated at https://drones.mil. Interested industry vendors capable of delivering commercial or dual-use maritime unmanned surface systems are encouraged to ensure active SAM.gov registrations and monitor this notice for amendments, industry day announcements, and formal AOI documentation. All inquiries concerning this notice must be submitted in writing to the Agreements Officer at Christopher.j.murr.civ@us.navy.mil (note this email is distinct/different than the auto generated SAM.gov). ______________________________________________________________________________________________________________Update_as_of_23_September_2026_______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ DRPM RAS is issuing this Call For Solutions (CFS) under the Drone Marketplace Commercial Solutions Opening W58RGZ26SC001. The CFS posting is in place of the aforementioned Area of Interest (AOI), a separate AOI will not be posted. title: Herring Biological Sampling
description: Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO) requires laboratory services to process biological samples collected from British Columbia (BC) commercial herring fisheries, test fisheries, and research activities. The biological information obtained through sample processing supports annual stock assessments and the development of scientific advice regarding the status of BC herring stocks. The Contractor will be required to provide all qualified personnel, laboratory facilities, equipment, materials, and services necessary to process approximately 200 to 250 herring samples per year. Each sample typically contains approximately 100 fish, although sample sizes may vary. The Contractor must process all samples provided by DFO, including samples containing fewer than 100 fish, in accordance with DFO-approved scientific procedures. For each fish processed, the Contractor must record the fish's length, weight, sex, gonad length, gonad weight, maturity stage, and one suitable herring scale for subsequent age determination. All sample identification information and biological data must be entered into the MS Access database provided by DFO. The Contractor must also prepare herring scale slides, maintain daily electronic data backups, conduct quality control checks, and submit the required data and associated materials within the specified timelines. The Contractor must provide a minimum two-person team consisting of one Project Manager and one Sampling Technician. The team must be available to process a minimum of five herring samples per day, with each sample containing approximately 100 fish. The Contractor must provide an appropriate laboratory facility with suitable workspace, equipment, cold-storage capacity, water supply, sanitation, and arrangements for the proper disposal of biological waste. Where the facility is located more than 10 km from the Pacific Biological Station (PBS), the Contractor will be responsible for arranging and paying for the pickup and transportation of samples from PBS to the facility. Processing activities are anticipated to take place annually between March 1 and May 15, with all processing completed by May 15 unless otherwise authorized by the DFO Project Authority. The Contractor must coordinate sample receipt or pickup with DFO, provide weekly submissions of prepared herring scale slides and original sample labels during the processing period, and return cleaned, empty sample buckets strapped in groups of ten. Daily electronic data backups must be completed using the USB drive provided by DFO. The Contractor must provide a completed MS Access database containing all required biological and sample information, prepared herring scale slides suitable for subsequent age determination, original sample labels, electronic data backup files, and cleaned sample buckets. All work must be performed in accordance with DFO's Procedures for Collecting and Processing British Columbia Herring Samples and any additional instructions provided by the DFO Project Authority. The initial Contract period and each option year are expected to require similar services and sample-processing volumes. The actual number of samples provided may vary according to sample availability. Payment will be made only for samples provided by DFO and services completed in accordance with the Statement of Work. The Contractor is responsible for all costs associated with performing the work, including personnel, facilities, equipment, materials, transportation where required, and waste disposal. All proposed personnel must be fluent in English and capable of understanding technical instructions, following scientific procedures, and communicating effectively with DFO personnel.

title: Belgium – Construction work – Bouwen van FacThory 2/3 te Genk
description: Deze opdracht betreft de realisatie van een bedrijfsverzamelgebouw voor de innovatieve maakeconomie FacThory 2/3 te Genk in opdracht van Mo-Thor NV. De opdracht wordt onderverdeeld in volgende vijf delen: Deel 1, ruwbouw, afwerking en algemene coördinatie der werken Dit deel omvat alle voorbereiding van het bouwterrein, grondwerken, structuurwerken, metselwerken, rioleringswerken, dakwerken en buitenschrijnwerk. Alle afwerkingen zoals pleisterwerken, lichte wanden, systeemwanden, vloerafwerkingen en plafonds, binnenschrijnwerk, vaste uitrustingen en schilderwerken, … (niet limitatief), maken eveneens deel uit van dit deel. De coördinatieopdracht, zijnde alle taken en verantwoordelijkheden die betrekking hebben op de coördinatie in tijd en ruimte tussen de verschillende delen van de Opdracht, behoort eveneens tot het takenpakket van de Aannemer. Deel 2, elektriciteit, data en veiligheidsinstallaties Dit deel omvat alle elektrische -, data- en veiligheidsinstallaties binnen en buiten het gebouw. De aannemer aan wie dit deel van de werken wordt toegewezen, en die als onderaannemer van de algemene hoofdaannemer zal optreden, zal als Aangeduide Onderaannemer worden vermeld in de Aanvraag tot Deelneming, voor zover deze voor de Kandidaat noodzakelijk is om aan de kwalitatieve selectievoorwaarden te voldoen. Deel 3, HVAC, sanitair en brandbestrijdingsinstallaties Dit deel omvat alle verwarmings-, ventilatie- en luchtbehandelingsinstallaties met inbegrip van alle elektrische voorzieningen hiertoe, alsook het gebouwbeheersysteem. Daarnaast omvat dit deel alle sanitaire- en brandbeveiligingsinstallaties binnen en buiten het gebouw met inbegrip van de pompinstallaties en alle elektrische voorzieningen hiertoe. Ook de sprinklerinstallatie maakt deel uit van dit deel. De aannemer aan wie dit deel van de werken wordt toegewezen, en die als onderaannemer van de algemene hoofdaannemer zal optreden, zal als Aangeduide Onderaannemer worden vermeld in de Aanvraag tot Deelneming, voor zover deze voor de Kandidaat noodzakelijk is om aan de kwalitatieve selectievoorwaarden te voldoen. Ter info wordt hierbij meegedeeld dat er zal aangesloten worden op een bestaande KWO-installatie. Deel 4, liften Dit deel omvat de liftinstallaties binnen het project. De aannemer aan wie dit deel van de werken wordt toegewezen, en die als onderaannemer van de algemene hoofdaannemer zal optreden, zal als Aangeduide Onderaannemer worden vermeld in de Aanvraag tot Deelneming, voor zover deze voor de Kandidaat noodzakelijk is om aan de kwalitatieve selectievoorwaarden te voldoen. Deel 5, omgevingsaanleg Dit deel omvat onder meer de grondwerken ten behoeve van de terreinaanleg, terreinverhardingen en bijhorende rioleringswerken, groenaanleg en buitensignalisatie (niet limitatief). De aannemer aan wie dit deel van de werken wordt toegewezen, en die als onderaannemer van de algemene hoofdaannemer zal optreden, zal als Aangeduide Onderaannemer worden vermeld in de Aanvraag tot Deelneming, voor zover deze voor de Kandidaat noodzakelijk is om aan de kwalitatieve selectievoorwaarden te voldoen. De te realiseren gebouwen en infrastructuur, de visie, gehanteerde uitgangspunten en beoogde doelstellingen, het voorziene materiaalgebruik en uitvoeringswijze, worden bondig toegelicht inde Projectdefinitie, dewelke als Bijlage 6 bij deze Selectieleidraad is gevoegd. Daarnaast wordt het aanvraagdossier voor stedenbouwkundige vergunning (enkel de plannen) als Bijlage 7 bij deze Selectieleidraad gevoegd, zodat de Kandidaten zich een beeld kunnen vormen van de beoogde realisatie, doch louter ter informatie en zonder dat de Kandidaten hieraan enige rechten kunnen ontlenen.

description: SOLICITATION UPDATE � OCTOBER 30, 2026 The Federal Bureau of Prisons, Federal Prison Camp - Bryan, is extending the quotation submission deadline for Solicitation 15B50427Q00000001 to Monday, November 16, 2026, at 11:00 a.m. Eastern Time (10:00 a.m. Central Time). This extension is being provided to allow the Government additional time to review and respond to questions received from prospective quoters. Notice of Combined Synopsis/Solicitation This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products prepared in accordance with the applicable Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 12 procedures. This announcement constitutes the solicitation; quotations are requested, and no separate written solicitation will be issued beyond the RFQ documents included in this posting. This acquisition is a 100% total small business set-aside. The solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference and in full text as provided in Attachment 2. The current text of Federal Acquisition Regulation provisions and clauses is available at https://www.acquisition.gov/. Requirement The Federal Bureau of Prisons, Federal Prison Camp - Bryan, seeks a responsible small business to supply and deliver two (2) 25-ton single-packaged air-conditioning units with gas heat, 208/230V, three-phase, 60 Hz, for Government installation at the ICC Building. This is a supply-and-delivery-only acquisition; installation is not included. Equipment and materials shall conform to Attachment 3, Statement of Work/Specifications. Quotations shall identify the manufacturer and model of the proposed units and include complete manufacturer product data sheets and specifications demonstrating compliance with the SOW. The Government-approved SOW controls the technical requirement. Delivery destination: Federal Bureau of Prisons, FPC Bryan, 1100 Ursuline Avenue, Bryan, TX 77803. Deliveries may be received Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m., excluding Federal holidays, as stated in the SOW. FOB destination. Quoters shall expressly provide their proposed delivery date. Acquisition and quotation requirements NAICS: 333415 (size standard shown in Attachment 2: 1,250 employees). Product Service Code: 4120. Contract type: firm-fixed-price. Vendors shall submit a completed SF 1449 (Attachment 2), firm-fixed unit and extended prices for both units including delivery, manufacturer/model identification, complete technical literature, and a proposed delivery date. Vendors must satisfy applicable small business eligibility requirements, including any applicable nonmanufacturer rule. Quotations shall be emailed to r3phillips@bop.gov. Faxed and hand-delivered quotations will not be accepted. The quotation email subject should identify RFQ 15B50427Q00000001. Questions shall be submitted in writing to the same email address. Any material clarification or change will be published as an amendment on SAM.gov. Quoters are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for amendments. Quotation deadline: November 4, 2026, at 11:00 a.m. Eastern Time Questions deadline: October 29, 2026, at 11:00 a.m. Eastern Time Basis for award The Government intends to make one firm-fixed-price award to the responsible, eligible small business whose quotation represents the best value to the Government, considering (1) Technical Acceptability, (2) Delivery Schedule, and (3) Price. Technical compliance will be evaluated against the SOW based on submitted manufacturer literature. Delivery will be evaluated against the quoter�s proposed schedule; an earlier achievable delivery date may provide additional value. Technical Acceptability and Delivery Schedule, combined, are more important than Price. The Government may select a higher-priced quotation where documented technical or delivery benefits justify the premium, or a lower-priced quotation when such benefits do not justify additional cost. The Government may make award without discussions. Registration, funding and payment Quoters must comply with the SAM.gov registration and representation requirements applicable to this solicitation and award. The Government will verify registration, exclusions, responsibility, and small-business eligibility before award. Issuance of this RFQ does not obligate the Government to make an award or reimburse quotation preparation costs. title: Digital Repository Platform and Physical Library Management System
description: The Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration is seeking information from interested parties and potential vendors and systems integrators to implement a web-based Digital Repository (Virtual Library) Platform integrated with specialized Physical Library Management functionality. The primary purpose of this platform is to serve as a centralized hub providing standardized access to industry consensus standards, regulatory documentation, and reference literature applicable to LNG facility safety. The platform should allow access through IP verification or username/password, support concurrent users, and not require any additional software to be installed on the user�s computer or server. The solution must seamlessly handle distinct tier-based access controls across geographically dispersed stakeholder groups, support concurrent platform usage, enforce digital rights management (DRM), track visitor engagement, and provide administrative reporting for PHMSA management. description: W912EE - The United States Army Corps of Engineers, Vicksburg District, intends to issue an Invitation for Bids (IFB) Solicitation Number W912EE27BA001 for the Lease of One Cutterhead, Hydraulic Pipeline Dredge (Not Less than 18-Inch Diameter), Fully Operated with Attendant Plant and Personnel, and with a Draft Not to Exceed 9 Feet, for Construction and Maintenance Dredging within the Vicksburg District � Mississippi River Ports and Harbors. The project has a completion period of 365 Calendar Days from the date of the Notice to Proceed. This IFB will be for one (1) Firm Fixed-Price Construction Contract. Bidders may register on the Interested Vendor's List (IVL) at https://sam.gov/ and retrieve an IVL from the same location. Compact disc and hard copies will not be available. Amendments, if/when issued, will be posted to the above referenced website for electronic downloading. This will be the only method of distributing amendments prior to closing. Bidders must have and maintain an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) at http://sam.gov and must include the NAICS code they are bidding under to receive a Government contract award. If the bidder is a Joint Venture (JV), the JV entity shall have valid SAM registration in the SAM database representing the JV as one business/firm/entity. If at the time of award a bidder is not actively and successfully registered in the SAM database, the Government reserves the right to award to the next prospective bidder. For additional information regarding this solicitation, please contact Andrew McCaskill via email at andrew.mccaskill@usace.army.mil. Technical inquiries and questions relating to the solicitation are to be submitted via Bidder Inquiry in ProjNet at www.projnet.org when the solicitation is made available. The solicitation, including any amendments, shall establish the official opening and closing dates and times. SOLICITATION ISSUE DATE ON OR ABOUT 16 NOVEMBER 2026. BID OPENING DATE AND TIME ON OR ABOUT 16 DECEMBER 2026, 1400 CENTRAL TIME. THIS PROCUREMENT IS ADVERTISED AS UNRESTRICTED. IT IS ISSUED UNDER NAICS 237990, PSC Z1KF, FOR ONE (1) FIRM FIXED-PRICE CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT.

title: R402--Real Estate Acquisition Support Services (REASS) Recompete
description: Notice of VISN-Based Solicitation Structure Since release of the prior draft solicitation, the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) has refined the acquisition strategy for Real Estate Acquisition Support Services to align with the Veterans Health Administration�s (VHA) evolving regional operating model. This revised approach supports VA�s broader Restructure for Impact and Sustainability Effort (RISE), an organizational transformation directed by Executive Order 14210. RISE is intended to streamline VHA structures and processes, strengthen regional implementation and accountability, and support more consistent, coordinated, and responsive services for Veterans. Accordingly, VA has transitioned from a single nationwide contractor-pool approach to a multiple-award IDIQ structure organized by Veterans Integrated Service Network (VISN) Coverage Area. Benefits of the VISN-based approach include: Allowing qualified SDVOSB offerors to compete for one or more VISN Coverage Areas rather than requiring a nationwide proposal; Enabling offerors to focus proposals on geographic areas where they can demonstrate staffing, local-market resources, capacity, and lawful authority to operate; Supporting focused competition and VISN-specific commission pricing; Improving alignment between broker support, VA regional lease-acquisition operations, and local-market requirements; Strengthening accountability for contractor capacity, performance, quality control, and continuity of services within each VISN Coverage Area; and Supporting VA�s broader effort to simplify operations, improve consistency, and enable more effective implementation at the regional and local levels. VA considered feedback received during the draft-solicitation/RFI phase. However, because the solicitation has been materially revised since the draft-solicitation/RFI phase, VA is not posting the historical draft-stage questions and Government responses. Those historical responses may not reflect the requirements, proposal instructions, evaluation approach, or procedures in the final solicitation. The final solicitation, its attachments, and any written amendments issued by the Contracting Officer are the only authoritative sources for solicitation requirements. Offerors shall submit questions concerning the final solicitation in accordance with the solicitation�s instructions.

title: R402--Real Estate Acquisition Support Services (REASS) Recompete
description: 36C10F20R0073 Presolicitation Notice Lease Acquisition Support Services (New Broker IDIQ) This is a presolicitation announcement for the Department of Veteran Affairs (VA), Office of Construction and Facilities Management (CFM). A Request for Proposal (RFP) will be issued on this Federal Business Opportunities (www.fbo.gov) website after 15 days after the release of this Notice. Lease Acquisition Support Services are required for a multiple award Broker Services Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract. This multiple award is set-aside for small businesses which will including Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) or Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB) on a tiered evaluation. The firms must be a licensed leasing broker with an approved NAICS Code of 531210. The intent is to award nine (9) contracts; however, awards may vary dependent on the best interest of the Government. The term will be one (1) base year and four (4) one-year option periods at the discretion of the Government. The minimum guarantee amount for the base period is $1,000.00. The contract will be a firm fixed-price IDIQ contract with a maximum amount of $30,000,000.00 per awardee over the contract period. The determination of acquisition strategy lies solely with the Government. All firms are cautioned to review the restrictions of FAR 9.5 Organizational and Consultant Conflicts of Interest. Any broker services firm that receives a request for proposal (RFP) for broker services will be restricted from participating in any other contract or task order for that particular project. This contract will be procured in accordance with FAR Part 15, this procurement is best value with tradeoffs. Firms must have an established working office and must be capable of responding to and working on multiple task orders concurrently. The Performance Work Statement (PWS) will include: Module 1 Lease Acquisition Support Services, CLIN 0001 thru 0004 will be commission fee. The Contracting Officer will determine whether to procure task orders for Module 1 services using CLIN 0001 thru 0004. Only CLIN 0001 thru 0004 will be allowed for module 1 lease acquisition services at the Task Order level. The services described below may include all or a combination of the following steps: 1) participating in a project orientation with the PM and LCO, other Government personnel, and other contractors; 2) providing GREX support; 3) advertising the requirement; 4) surveying the market and preparing a market survey report; 5) drafting issuing a LCO approved RLP and any RLP amendments; 6) conducting administrative reviews of offers; 7) inputting proposal financial data into analysis tools for LCO analysis and evaluation; 8) providing support to LCO in negotiations and discussions with offerors; 9) preparing the lease documents and any lease amendments, and coordinating required signatures; 10) coordinate Acceptance Inspection; and 11) support to VA with FOIA inquiries, Congressional and other governmental inquiries, claims, litigation, settlements, and disputes. The Contractor must hold a current state broker license in the United States of America OR Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. Additionally, in order to be awarded a lease acquisition TO, the Contractor must provide a broker license covering the state where the lease is being performed. Module 2 Lease Related Acquisition Support Services, CLIN 0005 as described in the PWS. Related services include User Group Design Meetings with Lessor; Lessor's Tenant Improvement (TI) Pricing Review; Change Orders; Construction Schedule and Initial Construction Meeting; Construction Progress Reporting; Coordination of VA Occupancy; Pre-Acceptance Submissions, Market research and analysis; Disputes, Protests, Claims, and Appeals, Congressional Inquiries, and FOIA Inquiries; Disputes/Protests, Claims/Appeals; and FOIA/Congressional/Other Inquiries. Module 3 Due Diligence Services, CLIN 0006, the Government requires certain due diligence studies prior to the award of a lease. Application of lesser requirements than what are listed in this Contract or in the PWSs provided must be approved by the Lease Contracting Officer within the Task Order on a case-by-case basis, in writing. The Contractor is responsible for verifying that all subcontractors possess industry-specific qualifications as required by Federal, State and local jurisdictions and licensing bodies. Subcontractors that do not possess the required qualifications shall not be utilized. The Contractor is also responsible for vetting subcontractors for potential conflicts of interest and for subcontractors compliance with access agreements and other arrangements between the Government and other landowners pertaining to use, access, and restoration activities. This contract will be procured in accordance with FAR Part 15, this procurement is best value with tradeoffs. The Government intends to award without discussions but reserves the right to conduct discussions. Competitive best value trade off source selection procedures will be used to evaluate proposals. Award will be made to responsible firm(s) offering the best value to the Government after evaluation of technical factors, past performance and total evaluated price including base and all option periods. Offerors must meet the mandatory minimum requirements of the solicitation and proposals must be submitted in the requested format and adhere to the specified page limitations Address all questions in writing to the issuing office via email to Catalin.Parfenti@va.gov with the Subject Line: 36C10F20R0073 | Lease Acquisition Support Services. No fax or telephone inquiries will be answered. No other information regarding scope, dates, etc. is available until issuance of the solicitation. --- End ---

The Library is the main research arm of the U.S. Congress and the home of the U.S. Copyright Office. The Library preserves and provides access to a rich, diverse and enduring source of knowledge to inform, inspire and engage visitors in their intellectual and creative endeavors. The Center for Exhibits and Interpretation (CEI) supports the Library�s mission by creating exhibits and publications that forge meaningful connections with the Library�s vast collections. Within CEI, the Exhibits Office (EO) is responsible for the design, fabrication, installation and maintenance of all components of the permanent and changing exhibitions at the Library. On behalf of the Library/CEI, EO seeks an experienced museum exhibit design firm for a full-service design of its upcoming changing exhibit Comics for its SW Gallery, approximately 3,700 SF, including one rotational package, and promotional graphics (one brochure, one poster design, and three website graphic designs as described below). The Comics changing exhibit will feature the Library�s unrivaled collections of comic books and related ephemera to explore their power as a storytelling medium and cultural icon. This exhibit will showcase a wide array of objects, images, and stories from the Library�s collections (and potential incoming loans) to tell the unique story of comics. AV integration and media production is not within the scope of this contract and will be subject to a separate contract. The Contractor shall provide expert quality creative exhibit design services for the Library�s Comics changing exhibition.

title: R402--Real Estate Acquisition Support Services (REASS) Recompete
description: Notice of VISN-Based Solicitation Structure Since release of the prior draft solicitation, the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) has refined the acquisition strategy for Real Estate Acquisition Support Services to align with the Veterans Health Administration s (VHA) evolving regional operating model. This revised approach supports VA s broader Restructure for Impact and Sustainability Effort (RISE), an organizational transformation directed by Executive Order 14210. RISE is intended to streamline VHA structures and processes, strengthen regional implementation and accountability, and support more consistent, coordinated, and responsive services for Veterans. Accordingly, VA has transitioned from a single nationwide contractor-pool approach to a multiple-award IDIQ structure organized by Veterans Integrated Service Network (VISN) Coverage Area. Benefits of the VISN-based approach include: Allowing qualified SDVOSB offerors to compete for one or more VISN Coverage Areas rather than requiring a nationwide proposal; Enabling offerors to focus proposals on geographic areas where they can demonstrate staffing, local-market resources, capacity, and lawful authority to operate; Supporting focused competition and VISN-specific commission pricing; Improving alignment between broker support, VA regional lease-acquisition operations, and local-market requirements; Strengthening accountability for contractor capacity, performance, quality control, and continuity of services within each VISN Coverage Area; and Supporting VA s broader effort to simplify operations, improve consistency, and enable more effective implementation at the regional and local levels. VA considered feedback received during the draft-solicitation/RFI phase. However, because the solicitation has been materially revised since the draft-solicitation/RFI phase, VA is not posting the historical draft-stage questions and Government responses. Those historical responses may not reflect the requirements, proposal instructions, evaluation approach, or procedures in the final solicitation. The final solicitation, its attachments, and any written amendments issued by the Contracting Officer are the only authoritative sources for solicitation requirements. Offerors shall submit questions concerning the final solicitation in accordance with the solicitation s instructions.

title: Request for Information (RFI) � Combat Rubber Raiding Craft (CRRC) Outboard Motors
description: This Sources Sought Synopsis (SSS)/Request for Information (RFI) is issued for informational purposes and market research only; it does not constitute a solicitation. The Government will not reimburse any company or individual for any expenses associated with preparing/submitting information in response to this posting. The information provided may be used by the Government in developing its acquisition strategy, statement of work/statement of objectives, and/or performance specifications. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary or competition sensitive information contained within their response as instructed later in this posting. The United States (US) Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC), Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance & Special Operations Forces (ISR & SOF) Directorate, Special Warfare (SW) Program Office (AFLCMC/WISN) is conducting market research to identify possible sources capable of providing a CRRC Outboard Motor (OE). The current Guardian Angel (GA) weapon system relies on CRRC Outboard Motors that are nearing the end of their service life and no longer fully meet the evolving requirements of the Personnel Recover (PR) mission. The obsolescence of the current motor fleet restricts operational capabilities and increases mission risk. Specifically, the inability to operate reliably in rough seas limits the ability to conduct PR missions in certain geographic locations and weather conditions. The current program lacks a viable replacement solution that addresses these deficiencies, restores the weapon system�s full operational capability, and provides GA personnel with a reliable and effective CRRC-system for all operational environments. Furthermore, the decreased horsepower and increased unit weight of modern potential replacement EPA compliant 4-stroke Outboard Motors (OE) reduce operational capability and aerial delivery mission flexibility. PLEASE SEE ATTACHMENT FOR ADDITIONAL DETAILS AND INFORMATION ON HOW TO RESPOND TO THIS RFI.

description: Horse Racing Ireland (HRI) was established by the Irish Government under the Horse and Greyhound Racing Act 2001 and the Irish Horseracing Industry Act 1994. Horse Racing Ireland (HRI) is seeking to purchase new Starting Stalls from suitably qualified suppliers for use at numerous racecourses over the Flat Racing Calendar. This framework maybe used for the supply of Starting Stalls for Horse Racing Ireland and its affiliates / associates, for up to 20 racecourses in the Republic of Ireland. title: Land Mobile Radio Infrastructure Maintenance and Support
description: Description Notice of Intent to Sole Source 1. Procurement Office Background The Mission and Installation Contracting Command - Yuma Proving Ground (MICC-YPG), on behalf of the U.S. Army Yuma Proving Ground (USAYPG), Yuma, Arizona, is conducting market research to identify potential sources capable of meeting the requirement described herein. This notice is issued to attempt to bolster government and industry coordination and partnership, as well as to determine if any other qualified commercial entities possess the capabilities to fulfill this requirement. 2. Scope of Requirement & Sole Source Intent The Government intends to award a Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) contract on a sole-source basis to Motorola Solutions, Inc. (809 Pinnacle Dr Ste G, Linthicum Heights, MD, 21090-2535). USAYPG currently operates an aging, proprietary Motorola Land Mobile Radio (LMR) network system (P25 digital system) manufactured by Motorola Solutions, Inc. This requirement is for the procurement of infrastructure maintenance and support subscription services, which include: Advanced Services & Cyber Support: 24/7/365 remote technical support provided via Motorola�s secure Operations Center. Diagnostics & Restorations: Real-time network management tools and OEM-level diagnostics capable of identifying, resolving, and restoring operations during critical system failures. Advanced Repair & Return (ARR): Quick-turnaround hardware repair and return services for proprietary LMR parts and components. On-line Technical Support: Tier-3/4 technical escalations beyond the capabilities of YPG organic personnel. Due to the proprietary nature of the P25 digital system and the significant Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) resources required for configuration management and information assurance, the government has determined that only Motorola Solutions, Inc. can provide these required sustainment services. This ensures that the network configuration remains in full compliance with Information Assurance requirements in accordance with Department of Defense Instruction (DoDI) 8500. 3. Information Sought (Capability Statement) If your firm possesses the capability to meet or exceed these requirements, the Government requests that you submit a Capability Statement demonstrating your technical and operational capacity. Please address the following inquiries in your response: OEM Support & Technical Capability: Describe your company's technical capability to provide 24/7 remote support, complex diagnostics, and physical parts repair/return for an aging proprietary Motorola P25 LMR network system. OEM Partnership & Authorization: Identify whether your firm is an authorized service provider or partner of Motorola Solutions, Inc., and clarify if your firm has the necessary agreements to utilize proprietary OEM diagnostics, software patches, and configuration tools. Information Assurance (DoDI 8500): Detail your technical approach to ensuring the LMR system remains in full compliance with DoD Information Assurance requirements under DoDI 8500. Commerciality: Does your company believe this infrastructure maintenance and support subscription service is a commercial item/service under FAR Part 12? NAICS Suitability: Do you agree that NAICS code 811210 (Communication Equipment Repair and Maintenance Services) is the most appropriate classification for this acquisition? If not, please propose an alternative NAICS code with justification. Socioeconomic Status & Business Size: Identify your business size standard under NAICS 811210 (e.g., Small Business, 8(a), HUBZone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business, Women-Owned Small Business, or Large Business). Acquisition Approach: Identify whether your firm is interested in competing for this requirement as a Prime Contractor, or if you would pursue a subcontracting, joint-venture, or teaming arrangement. THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) IS SOLELY FOR INFORMATION AND PLANNING PURPOSES. It does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP), Request for Quotes (RFQ), or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. The Government is not seeking proposals at this time and will not accept unsolicited proposals. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI; all costs associated with responding will be solely at the interested party�s expense. The Government is interested in input from the small business community across all socioeconomic categories (including 8(a), Small Disadvantaged Business, HUBZone, SDVOSB, and WOSB) to identify their capabilities in meeting the requirement at a fair market price. Any information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. NAICS Details Proposed services are classified under NAICS code 811210 - Communication Equipment Repair and Maintenance Services with the Corresponding index entry Communication Equipment Repair and Maintenance Services (Size Standard: $34.0M). This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in repairing and maintaining communications equipment without retailing new communications equipment, such as commercial two-way radios, cellular/mobile phones, and carrier-line transmission equipment. Attachments: Draft Performance Work Statement (PWS)

title: F108--620-26-206 Asbestos Abatement
description: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office (NCO) 2, intends to issue Solicitation 36C24227R0010 for Project 620-26-206 Asbestos Abatement at Montrose VA Medical Center, 2094 Albany Post Rd, Montrose, NY 10548. This notice is for pre-solicitation purposes only and is issued to provide advance notice of the Government's intent to solicit this construction requirement. This notice is not a request for quotes, proposals, or bids, and no contract award will be made as a result of this announcement. The official solicitation is anticipated to be posted on or about November 6, 2026, on SAM.gov, at which time all solicitation documents, including the Statement of Work, drawings, specifications, and proposal submission instructions, will be made available. This procurement is anticipated to be issued as a 100% Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) set-aside. Eligible SDVOSBs are encouraged to submit an offer upon release of the solicitation. All prospective offerors must be currently registered in www.sam.gov, www.dnb.com (Duns and Bradstreet) and be registered and verified as a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) in https://search.certifications.sba.gov/ at the time of offer submission and before award of this procurement. The applicable NAICS Code is 562910 with a small business size standard of $25.0 million. The Magnitude of Construction for this project is between $100,000 and $250,000. Scope of Work: The Montrose VA Medical Center anticipates awarding a construction contract for asbestos abatement in the Building 3 Physical Therapy/Sleep Study area. The project involves asbestos abatement within an approximately 2,300-square-foot area, including approximately 100 square feet of radiator heat shielding. Work includes the removal and proper disposal of friable and non-friable asbestos-containing materials (ACM), associated demolition, utility modifications, and site restoration as required by the contract drawings and specifications. The Contractor shall furnish all necessary labor, materials, equipment, supervision, and services to complete the work in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local regulations, including VA safety and infection-control requirements and New York State asbestos-abatement regulations. Work may require evening or weekend operations to minimize disruption to facility occupants. Period of Performance: The period of performance for Abatement shall be 365 days from Notice to Proceed (NTP). All other details and information shall be contained in the solicitation which shall be posted on www.sam.gov. The response submittal address, date and time will be included in the solicitation

Bidders must have and maintain an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) at http://sam.gov and must include the NAICS code they are bidding under to receive a Government contract award. If the bidder is a Joint Venture (JV), the JV entity shall have valid SAM registration in the SAM database representing the JV as one business/firm/entity. If at the time of award a bidder is not actively and successfully registered in the SAM database, the Government reserves the right to award to the next prospective bidder. title: SB ERS MATOC, USACE Northwestern Division and EPA Region 2
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Kansas City District is procuring a Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) for Environmental Remediation Services (ERS) in support of United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Northwestern Division (NWD) and the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Region 2. The MATOC will be procured on a competitive basis as a total small business (SB) set-aside under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 562910 Environmental Remediation Services. The scope of the SB ERS MATOC includes in-situ thermal remediation, in-situ chemical oxidation, and other chemical stabilization of contamination; operations and maintenance of remediation systems including large scale groundwater treatment plants, soil vapor extraction systems, and air sparge systems; preparation of work plans; studies with associated reports; multiple phases of field investigations; preliminary assessments; site inspections and remedial site inspections; remedial investigations; feasibility studies; Engineering Evaluation Cost Analysis; monitoring well installation and sampling; short and long term monitoring/long term operations or Long Term Response Action (LTRA); data management; data interpretation; engineering evaluation and corrective actions; optimization studies; ground-water modeling; geophysical surveys; remediation cost estimates; management of non-hazardous and hazardous investigative derived waste; environmental and human health risk assessments; risk based remediation; air emission issues including vapor intrusion; surface water discharge; applying for environmental permits; remedial design; well abandonment; meetings; public meeting participation; preparation of presentation material both written and visual; hydrological, sediment and soil studies; project reports; engineering support and/or design; value engineering studies; operations and maintenance for hazardous, toxic, and radioactive waste (HTRW) sites; energy evaluations for remediation systems; remedial action plans; remedial actions; removal action plans; removal actions; construction support; site closeout/decision documents; abandoned mines program support; and future project programming and scheduling support. The solicitation will be made available no earlier than 15 days after this presolicitation notice. All responsible sources may submit a proposal in response to the solicitation, which the government will consider in the award decision. This notice does not constitute a commitment on the part of the Government to award a contract, nor to pay for any costs incurred as a result in replying to this notice. This notice should not be construed as a commitment by the Government for any purpose.

description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Kansas City District is procuring a Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) for Environmental Remediation Services (ERS) in support of United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Northwestern Division (NWD) and the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Region 2. The MATOC will be procured on a competitive basis as a total small business (SB) set-aside under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 562910 Environmental Remediation Services. The scope of the SB ERS MATOC includes in-situ thermal remediation, in-situ chemical oxidation, and other chemical stabilization of contamination; operations and maintenance of remediation systems including large scale groundwater treatment plants, soil vapor extraction systems, and air sparge systems; preparation of work plans; studies with associated reports; multiple phases of field investigations; preliminary assessments; site inspections and remedial site inspections; remedial investigations; feasibility studies; Engineering Evaluation Cost Analysis; monitoring well installation and sampling; short and long term monitoring/long term operations or Long Term Response Action (LTRA); data management; data interpretation; engineering evaluation and corrective actions; optimization studies; ground-water modeling; geophysical surveys; remediation cost estimates; management of non-hazardous and hazardous investigative derived waste; environmental and human health risk assessments; risk based remediation; air emission issues including vapor intrusion; surface water discharge; applying for environmental permits; remedial design; well abandonment; meetings; public meeting participation; preparation of presentation material both written and visual; hydrological, sediment and soil studies; project reports; engineering support and/or design; value engineering studies; operations and maintenance for hazardous, toxic, and radioactive waste (HTRW) sites; energy evaluations for remediation systems; remedial action plans; remedial actions; removal action plans; removal actions; construction support; site closeout/decision documents; abandoned mines program support; and future project programming and scheduling support. The solicitation will be made available no earlier than 15 days after this presolicitation notice. All responsible sources may submit a proposal in response to the solicitation, which the government will consider in the award decision. This notice does not constitute a commitment on the part of the Government to award a contract, nor to pay for any costs incurred as a result in replying to this notice. This notice should not be construed as a commitment by the Government for any purpose.

title: F108--620-26-206 Asbestos Abatement
description: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office (NCO) 2, intends to issue Solicitation 36C24227R0010 for Project 620-26-206 Asbestos Abatement at Montrose VA Medical Center, 2094 Albany Post Rd, Montrose, NY 10548. This notice is for pre-solicitation purposes only and is issued to provide advance notice of the Government's intent to solicit this construction requirement. This notice is not a request for quotes, proposals, or bids, and no contract award will be made as a result of this announcement. The official solicitation is anticipated to be posted on or about November 6, 2026, on SAM.gov, at which time all solicitation documents, including the Statement of Work, drawings, specifications, and proposal submission instructions, will be made available. This procurement is anticipated to be issued as a 100% Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) set-aside. Eligible SDVOSBs are encouraged to submit an offer upon release of the solicitation. All prospective offerors must be currently registered in www.sam.gov, www.dnb.com (Duns and Bradstreet) and be registered and verified as a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) in https://search.certifications.sba.gov/ at the time of offer submission and before award of this procurement. The applicable NAICS Code is 562910 with a small business size standard of $25.0 million. The Magnitude of Construction for this project is between $100,000 and $250,000. Scope of Work: The Montrose VA Medical Center anticipates awarding a construction contract for asbestos abatement in the Building 3 Physical Therapy/Sleep Study area. The project involves asbestos abatement within an approximately 2,300-square-foot area, including approximately 100 square feet of radiator heat shielding. Work includes the removal and proper disposal of friable and non-friable asbestos-containing materials (ACM), associated demolition, utility modifications, and site restoration as required by the contract drawings and specifications. The Contractor shall furnish all necessary labor, materials, equipment, supervision, and services to complete the work in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local regulations, including VA safety and infection-control requirements and New York State asbestos-abatement regulations. Work may require evening or weekend operations to minimize disruption to facility occupants. Period of Performance: The period of performance for Abatement shall be 365 days from Notice to Proceed (NTP). All other details and information shall be contained in the solicitation which shall be posted on www.sam.gov. The response submittal address, date and time will be included in the solicitation

title: SB ERS MATOC, USACE Northwestern Division and EPA Region 2
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Kansas City District is procuring a Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) for Environmental Remediation Services (ERS) in support of United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Northwestern Division (NWD) and the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Region 2. The MATOC will be procured on a competitive basis as a total small business (SB) set-aside under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 562910 Environmental Remediation Services. The scope of the SB ERS MATOC includes in-situ thermal remediation, in-situ chemical oxidation, and other chemical stabilization of contamination; operations and maintenance of remediation systems including large scale groundwater treatment plants, soil vapor extraction systems, and air sparge systems; preparation of work plans; studies with associated reports; multiple phases of field investigations; preliminary assessments; site inspections and remedial site inspections; remedial investigations; feasibility studies; Engineering Evaluation Cost Analysis; monitoring well installation and sampling; short and long term monitoring/long term operations or Long Term Response Action (LTRA); data management; data interpretation; engineering evaluation and corrective actions; optimization studies; ground-water modeling; geophysical surveys; remediation cost estimates; management of non-hazardous and hazardous investigative derived waste; environmental and human health risk assessments; risk based remediation; air emission issues including vapor intrusion; surface water discharge; applying for environmental permits; remedial design; well abandonment; meetings; public meeting participation; preparation of presentation material both written and visual; hydrological, sediment and soil studies; project reports; engineering support and/or design; value engineering studies; operations and maintenance for hazardous, toxic, and radioactive waste (HTRW) sites; energy evaluations for remediation systems; remedial action plans; remedial actions; removal action plans; removal actions; construction support; site closeout/decision documents; abandoned mines program support; and future project programming and scheduling support. The solicitation will be made available no earlier than 15 days after this presolicitation notice. All responsible sources may submit a proposal in response to the solicitation, which the government will consider in the award decision. This notice does not constitute a commitment on the part of the Government to award a contract, nor to pay for any costs incurred as a result in replying to this notice. This notice should not be construed as a commitment by the Government for any purpose.

title: Industry Day Announcement Supply Chain Illumination
description: Industry Day Announcement Air Force Life Cycle Management Center, Armament Directorate Supply Chain Illumination Capability Hosted by AFLCMC/EB BLUF: AFLCMC/EB requires a secure, scalable, AI-assisted federated data capability that integrates but not unnecessarily replaces existing government, Service, and contractor data sources. The capability must provide end-to-end supply-chain mapping, risk identification and assessment, near-real-time situational awareness, mitigation tracking, and evidence-based decision support for priority munition programs, initially within the Long-Range Weapons, Affordable Munition, and Adaptive Weapons portfolios, with potential expansion across the Armament Directorate portfolio. 1. Introduction The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC), Armament Directorate (EB), plans to conduct a virtual Industry Day to conduct market research and obtain industry feedback regarding a potential Supply Chain Illumination capability for the munitions enterprise. The Armament Directorate is pursuing an artificial intelligence-assisted, federated data capability to map critical munition supply chains to raw-material sources. The intended capability would provide enterprise-level visibility into supply-chain dependencies, bottlenecks, supplier risks, competing demands, and mitigation actions in support of senior-leader decision-making and mission outcomes. This Industry Day is intended to inform the Government�s market research under Federal Acquisition Regulation Part 10 and help identify mature, scalable commercial and non-traditional solutions that can support the Directorate�s supply-chain visibility requirements. This announcement does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), solicitation, commitment, or promise to issue a solicitation in the future. 2. Background The Armament Directorate currently lacks an integrated mechanism to assess critical supply-chain risk across its acquisition divisions, military Services, and contractor-supported weapon systems. Existing data sources are fragmented (data lives in siloed systems), contractor logistics support arrangements can limit visibility into multi-tier supply chains, and shared dependencies across military and commercial demand can create unanticipated production risk. The Government seeks to improve end-to-end visibility of materials, suppliers, production dependencies, single points of failure, foreign-source dependencies, and mitigation actions across priority munition portfolios down to the raw materials at the lowest of sub-tier suppliers. The initial proof of concept is expected to focus on PAE-prioritized programs within the Long-Range Weapons, Affordable Munition, and Adaptive Weapons portfolios, with potential expansion across the Armament Directorate weapon-system portfolio. 3. Industry Day Objectives The Government seeks industry feedback on approaches to establish a secure, scalable Supply Chain Illumination capability that can: Map supply chains from end item to raw-material origin for critical munition programs, through all tiers of subcontractors. Federate existing government, Service, and contractor data sources without unnecessarily replacing established systems. Identify and assess supply-chain risks, including bottlenecks, single points of failure, constrained materials, supplier financial and manufacturing risk, foreign influence, and competing demands. Support data-sharing standards and interfaces that protect legitimate competition sensitive information while providing the Government sufficient visibility for risk management and decision support. Enable near-real-time situational awareness through application programming interfaces and other appropriate data-exchange mechanisms. Apply AI-assisted analytics, including machine-learning and knowledge-graph approaches, to identify relationships, risks, and mitigation options across complex, multi-tier supply chains. Track mitigation actions through end-item delivery and produce evidence suitable for waiver assessments and senior-leader decision-making. Integrate with relevant enterprise architectures and platforms, including existing Air Force, Army, Navy, and digital Bill of Materials efforts, as appropriate. 4. Event Details for the Virtual Industry Day Open to All Contractors Date: 15 December 2026 Time: 0900hrs CST Location/Platform: Teams Link Classification: Unclassified Registration Deadline: 16 November 2026 The Government will provide an overview of the operational problem, desired endstate, preliminary technical considerations, and potential next steps. The agenda may also include question-and-answer sessions and opportunities for industry participants to provide oral or written feedback. 5. Registration and Participation Registration is required. Interested organizations should submit the following information no later than 16 November 2026: Company name Company address Attendee name, title, email address, and telephone number Identification of the company�s primary point of contact A brief description of the company�s relevant capability or experience Any requested accessibility or administrative support requirements Submit registration information to: SMO Code: AFLCMC EB, David Sanders (850) 883-1670. 6. Follow-On Engagement Following Industry Day, the Government may issue a Request for Information, schedule one-on-one market-research discussions, request white papers, or conduct other market-research activities for live demonstrated capabilities only. Participation in Industry Day is not required for participation in any future acquisition or market-research activity unless expressly stated in a future notice. 7. Individual Demonstration Sessions Although not required, contractors may request one-on-one discussions for the sole purpose of providing a live demonstration that addresses the following questions for munitions: Supply Chain Risk: Which suppliers, components, and lower-tier dependencies present the greatest risk to weapon system readiness and production schedules? Operational Performance: How do suppliers lead times, material availability, and supply chain disruptions influence production delays and repair turnaround times? Investment Prioritization: Which supply chain vulnerabilities should receive priority investment to improve production capacity, reduce delays, and strengthen operational readiness? Predictive Analytics: To what extent can historical supplier performance, component lead times, and material shortages predict future supply chain disruptions? To coordinate a one-on-one session with the Government, contract Bryant Callahan, as shown in paragraph 9. Any one-on-one session will be scheduled after the Virtual Industry Day on15 December 2026. 8. Informational Notice THIS IS AN INFORMATIVE POSTING. This announcement is issued solely for planning and market research purposes. It does not constitute RFP, solicitation, contract, or commitment by the Government to procure any supply or service. The Government is not requesting proposals currently. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs incurred in preparing or submitting registration materials, participating in Industry Day, providing feedback, or responding to any subsequent market research request. This language follows the informative-posting framework used in the supplied Industry Day announcement. 9. Point of Contact Primary Point of Contact: Bryant Callahan AFLCMC/EB bryant.callahan.3@us.af.mil 850-797-4770 Contracting Point of Contact: Patricia Chisholm patricia.chisholm@us.af.mil 850-882-6935

title: High Consequence Infectious Disease (HCID) Staff Training
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE High Consequence Infectious Disease Staff Training Notice ID: 36C24827Q0097 Agency: Department of Veterans Affairs Sub-tier: Veterans Health Administration Contracting Office: NCO8 Notice Type: Sources Sought Proposed Set-Aside: To Be Determined NAICS Code: 611430 Product Service Code: U009 Response Deadline: 11/16/2026, 2:00 P.M. EST Place of Performance: Orlando VA Medical Center, 13800 Veterans Way, Orlando, Florida 32827 1. Purpose This Sources Sought Notice is issued solely for market research and acquisition-planning purposes. The Department of Veterans Affairs is seeking information from qualified business concerns capable of providing High Consequence Infectious Disease (HCID) training to staff of the Orlando VA Healthcare System. The information received may be used to determine the availability and capability of prospective contractors, the commercial availability of the required services, and the appropriate acquisition strategy, including whether a socioeconomic set-aside is supportable. Federal market research is used to determine whether capable sources and commercial services exist. For VA acquisitions, market research also supports the determination of whether capable certified Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses or Veteran-Owned Small Businesses are likely to submit offers at fair and reasonable prices. 2. Disclaimer This notice is not a solicitation. It is not a Request for Proposal, Request for Quotation, Invitation for Bid, or commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. Responses will not be considered offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Submission of information is voluntary, and the Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparing or submitting a response. The Government is not obligated to provide respondents with the results of this market research. Respondents should not submit pricing proposals unless specifically requested below. Proprietary information should be clearly marked. The Government may use information received to refine its requirements and acquisition strategy. 3. Background The Orlando VA Healthcare System Emergency Management Service supports incident response and recovery operations involving natural and human-caused emergencies. Its mission includes coordination with Federal, State, local, Tribal, and territorial organizations during significant incidents and emergencies. The contemplated requirement would strengthen staff readiness to identify, manage, and respond safely to HCIDs while maintaining appropriate infection-prevention, occupational-safety, and patient-care practices. 4. Anticipated Scope The contractor would provide instructor-led virtual training and onsite practical training. The anticipated requirement includes the following components. 4.1 Virtual Interactive Training The contractor would conduct up to six virtual interactive classes, with no more than 50 participants per class, to train as many as 300 staff members. Anticipated subject areas include: HCID definitions, examples, epidemiology, and modes of transmission; Recognition, signs and symptoms, case definitions, and clinical presentation; Standard, contact, droplet, and airborne precautions; PPE selection and general donning and doffing procedures; Hand hygiene; Environmental cleaning and disinfection; Waste management; Patient isolation and transportation within the facility; Coordination with infection-prevention and public-health organizations; Safe specimen collection, packaging, and transportation; Post-exposure decontamination, reporting, prophylaxis, and monitoring; Occupational Health responsibilities; Risk communication, patient and family education, and reporting; Support for staff and patient emotional care; and Other related HCID preparedness topics identified by the Government. 4.2 Onsite Practical Training The contractor would conduct five onsite classes providing hands-on PPE donning and doffing instruction. Each class would contain no more than 15 participants, with practical training provided to a maximum of 60 staff members. The unused slots are designed to allow some flexibility to accommodate staffing schedles. Instruction would use a checklist-based method under which participants rotate between reading the procedure and demonstrating correct donning and doffing until competency is achieved. The Government anticipates providing the training PPE, including: 3M TR-600 powered air-purifying respirators; Tyvek 800 coveralls; Inner gloves; Extended-cuff outer gloves; Knee-high shoe covers; and Hospital scrubs. The contractor would also instruct participants on PPE-waste management and applicable post-exposure procedures. 4.3 Standards Training must be based on current authoritative guidance and comply with applicable requirements, including: Current Centers for Disease Control and Prevention guidance; OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Standard, 29 CFR 1910.1030; OSHA Personal Protective Equipment requirements, 29 CFR 1910.132; and OSHA Respiratory Protection Standard, 29 CFR 1910.134. 4.4 Schedule All courses are anticipated to be completed within 60 calendar days after contract award. Onsite training may occur outside normal business hours to accommodate staff schedules and may be scheduled over multiple consecutive days. Exact dates and times would be coordinated between the contractor and the designated VA point of contact. 5. Anticipated Contractor Responsibilities The contractor would be expected to: Provide qualified instructors with demonstrated HCID, infection-prevention, PPE, and adult-training experience. Conduct all virtual and onsite classes. Provide its own laptop and presentation equipment for onsite instruction because access to the VA computer network may not be available. Provide professionally prepared workbooks, handouts, manuals, and related instructional materials. Make virtual-training materials available electronically in PDF format. Maintain accurate attendance records. Provide completion certificates to participants. Assess each practical-training participant�s competency. Provide completed competency documentation to the participant and designated VA personnel. Administer participant feedback assessments at the end of each session. Summarize assessment results and provide the supporting feedback records to designated VA personnel. Monitor practical-training participants for signs of heat stress or other safety concerns while PPE is worn. Comply with applicable VA security, privacy, records-management, facility-access, and safety requirements. 6. Government-Furnished Support The Government anticipates: Coordinating mutually acceptable training dates and times; Providing suitable space for onsite classroom and practical instruction; Providing training PPE and related supplies; and Confirming that onsite participants are medically cleared before participating in PPE exercises. 7. Information Requested Interested organizations should submit a capability statement containing, at minimum: Business information Legal business name; Physical and mailing addresses; Website; Primary point of contact; Telephone number and email address; Unique Entity Identifier; Commercial and Government Entity code; and Current SAM.gov registration status. Business size and socioeconomic status Large or small business under the proposed NAICS code; Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business; Veteran-Owned Small Business; Women-Owned Small Business; Economically Disadvantaged Women-Owned Small Business; 8(a) participant; HUBZone small business; or Other applicable socioeconomic category. Technical capability A concise explanation of the firm�s ability to perform all virtual and onsite training requirements; Qualifications and relevant experience of proposed instructors; Experience delivering HCID, infection-prevention, respiratory-protection, and PPE competency training to healthcare professio
