title: C1DA--578-27-003 - Renovate A Section First Floor of Building 1 - Design FY27
description: AMENDMENT A0001 Combined Synopsis/Solicitation Notice Combined Synopsis/Solicitation Notice Combined Synopsis/Solicitation Notice REQUEST FOR SF 330 36C25227Q0013 Project 578-27-003: Renovate A Section 1st Floor Bldg. 1 (AE) Design/Engineering Services SF-330 Package Due: October 30, 2026, at 1:00 p.m. CST (see details below) Points of Contact: Donita.Grace@va.gov INTRODUCTION: THIS IS A TOTAL 100% SERVICE-DISABLED VETERAN-OWNED SMALL BUSINESS (SDVOSB) SET-ASIDE in accordance with Public Law 109-461. This is a Request for SF330s for Architect/Engineer (A/E) Design Services for Project Number 578-27-003: Renovate A Section 1st Floor Bldg. 1 (AE) at the Edward J. Hines VA Hospital in Hines, IL. THIS ANNOUNCEMENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. NO SOLICITATION PACKAGE WILL BE ISSUED via SAM.gov. A request for proposal will be issued directly to the top-rated firm for which negotiations will commence in accordance with FAR part 36. The anticipated A/E design services, to be awarded, will be procured in accordance with the Selection of Architects and Engineers Act (Public Law 92- 582), FAR Part 36.6 and VA Acquisition Regulation 836.6. Period of Performance: 449 Calendar Days Contract Type: Firm-Fixed-Price Estimated Magnitude of Construction: Between $10,000,000 and $20,000,000 NAICS Code: 541310 Size Standard: $12.5 Million SBA & SAM : in accordance with VAAR 819.7003, at the time of SF330 submission and prior to award of any contract, the offeror must represent to the contracting officer that it is a (1) SDVOSB eligible firm; (2) Small business concern under the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code assigned to the acquisition; and (3) SDVOSB listed as verified in SBA at: https://veterans.certify.sba.gov/ Additionally, all eligible firms must be registered and current in the System for Award Management (SAM) database to be evaluated and eligible for contract award. If the firm is not registered in SAM, you may register online at https://www.sam.gov. 1. PURPOSE: This Source Selection Plan (SSP) outlines the procedures that will be used to solicit architectural and engineering (AE) design services for Project 578-27-003 Renovate A Section on First Floor of Building 1. The goal of this project is to provide complete AE design services to renovate section A of the 1st floor of building 1. 2. ACQUISISTION DESCRIPTION: 2.1: RFI: A Request for Information shall be published to https://sam.gov whereby interested architect-engineering companies shall submit an SF330 package. This competitive procurement shall utilize a best value trade-off source selection process identified in FAR 15. 2.1.a: Source Selection Evaluation Board (SSEB): For the purpose of this acquisition, the SSEB will be same as the Technical Evaluation Board (TEB). 2.1.b: Below are the individual (TEB) evaluation criteria and ratings for the SF330s, listed in descending order of importance. FACTOR 1: SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE AND TECHNICAL COMPETENCE (30 Maximum Points) Subfactor 1A: Specialized Experience (15 Points). Subfactor 1B: Additional Experience (10 points). Subfactor 1C: Technical Competence (5 points). The A/E Firm shall demonstrate its specialized experience and technical competence in the design and construction period services for projects of similar size and complexity. Specialized project experience should include design of renovations to existing hospitals, renovations to buildings constructed prior to 1970 w/space constraints, design of Pathology Suites, and HVAC upgrades to existing hospitals. Additional experience includes mechanical, electrical, and structural engineering, architecture, interior design and finishes, physical security upgrades, building management systems/building automation systems (BMS/BAS), Computer-Aided Design and Drafting (CADD), critical path scheduling, fire protection, construction infection control protocols, design and installation of biological refrigeration and preservation systems, design and installation of vacuum tube transport systems, and project phasing and coordination in an active hospital setting. Offeror shall provide a minimum of three (3), and no more than five (5) recent and relevant Government and private experience projects similar in size, scope, and complexity, and experience with the type of projects/competence above. Relevant is defined as those task requirements identified in the Statement of Work. Recent is defined as services provided within the past seven (7) years with at least 50% of the Construction completed. At a minimum, include the following for each submitted project (if applicable): Project title, location, contract number, and detailed narrative describing the scope of services provided including the type of work performed by the offeror and its role in the project i.e., prime contract, Teaming Partner, or subcontractor. Project Owner, owner s point of contact including telephone number and email address. Services & Deliverables provided under the contract/task order Period of Performance, including start and completion dates for design and construction if applicable. Estimated cost of construction based on AE s design Final construction cost (or projected final construction cost if still underway) The percentage of total cost resulting from changes due to AE omissions. To demonstrate technical competence, the offeror shall include narratives of how the firm addresses each of the following topics. Simply restating this list will not be sufficient. The management approach The coordination of disciplines and subcontractors Quality control procedures Familiarity with VA Design Guides/Manuals, Master Specifications and other applicable standards. FACTOR 2: PROFESSIONAL QUALIFICATIONS (20 Maximum Points) Subfactor 2A: Key Positions (15 Points). Subfactor 2B: SDVOSB Compliance (5 Points). The architects and engineers on the firm s staff representing the project or signing/stamping drawings in each discipline must possess a minimum of five (5) years of experience and are required to be licensed, registered, or certified by a U.S. state, the District of Columbia, or a U.S. territory. Provide professional license jurisdiction of issue and license numbers and/or proof of licensure. A resume for each of these key positions must be provided, corresponding with the title matching the disciplines listed for the project. At a minimum, the offeror must describe the professional qualifications and specific experience in the required disciplines within the past five (5) years. Key positions and disciplines required for this project include, but are not limited to: Project Manager Architect Mechanical Engineer Electrical Engineer Plumbing Engineer Structural Engineer Interior Designer The evaluation will consider education, certifications, training, registration, overall and relevant experience and longevity with the firm. Offer must include the following statement of SDVOSB compliance when submitting the personnel proposed to perform the work under this requirement: I [signatory authority] ______________________, [company] _____________________; certify that the team proposed to perform under this requirement demonstrates the capability of 50% SDVOSB performance in compliance of 48 CFR 852.219-10. FACTOR 3: PAST PERFORMANCE (20 Maximum Points) Subfactor 3A: Past Performance of projects identified in FACTOR 1. (15 Points). Subfactor 3B: Average Past Performance of all projects (5 Points). Provide CPARS data for all projects identified in FACTOR 1. For any project that does NOT have CPARS data available, a Past Performance Questionnaire (PPQ) is required to be submitted with the SF330. Please utilize the attached PPQ document. CPARS data and PPQs will not be included in the page count. All projects provided in the SF330 must be completed by the office/ branch/ individual team member performing the work under this contract. I Background and Purpose: NAVFAC Washington / FEAD Quantico is conducting market research to determine the availability, capability, and capacity of qualified commercial contractors to provide complete basewide janitorial and custodial services across facilities located at Marine Corps Base (MCB) Quantico, Virginia. Current Acquisition Posture � This requirement is currently performed under an existing contract awarded through the Small Business Administration (SBA) 8(a) Business Development Program expiring on March 31, 2027. In accordance with the Small Business Act and federal acquisition regulations, the Government is primarily surveying the market to identify qualified and capable SBA-certified 8(a) small business concerns (including 8(a) single-entity, tribally-owned, ANC, or NHO participants) to assess whether a follow-on sole-source award or competitive 8(a) set-aside is the appropriate acquisition strategy. Secondarily, the Government invites capabilities statements from other SBA-certified socioeconomic small business categories (HUBZone, SDVOSB/VOSB, and WOSB/EDWOSB) to assess total small business industry capacity. II Summary Scope of Work: The Contractor shall provide all personnel, management, supervision, tools, equipment, transportation, materials, supplies, and quality control necessary to deliver comprehensive custodial and janitorial services at MCB Quantico facilities. Representative tasks include, but are not limited to: � Routine Cleaning & Sanitation: Daily cleaning, sanitizing, and restocking of restrooms, locker rooms, breakrooms, and common areas. � Surface Maintenance: Emptying trash, recycling receptacles, and bulk waste disposal. � Floor Care: Sweeping, dust-mopping, damp-mopping, buffing, and periodic stripping and waxing of hard surface floors. � Carpet Care: Routine vacuuming, spot cleaning, and periodic hot-water extraction deep cleaning. � Glass & Fixture Cleaning: Interior and exterior window cleaning, partition washing, and drinking fountain sanitization. � Security & Installation Access: Strict compliance with Department of the Navy and MCB Quantico physical security policies, including Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) credentialing for all personnel. III Submission Requirements (Capability Statement): Interested, qualified small business contractors capable of self-performing the required work are invited to submit a Capabilities Statement. The submission shall not exceed two (2) pages (excluding title page) and must address the following: A. Company Information 1. Company Name, Address, and Website. 2. Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Code and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI). 3. Primary and Alternate Points of Contact (Name, Title, Phone Number, and Email). 4. Location of local/branch offices within the DC-Maryland-Virginia (DMV) commuting radius. B. Socioeconomic & Business Status 5. Identification of business size under NAICS 561720 ($22.0M size standard). 6. Socioeconomic designations: Specifically declare whether the firm is an active SBA-certified 8(a) participant. If certified 8(a), state your 8(a) entrance and anticipated graduation/exit dates, as well as your assigned SBA Servicing District Office. 7. Other certifications (HUBZone, SDVOSB, VOSB, WOSB, EDWOSB, or Small Business). C. Capability & Performance Qualifications 8. Self-Performance Capacity: Confirmation of the firm�s ability to comply with FAR 52.219-14 (Limitations on Subcontracting), demonstrating that at least 50% of the cost of contract performance incurred for personnel will be expended on employees of the prime firm. 9. Installation Access & Clearance: Statement confirming capability to obtain DBIDS credentials and security vetting for on-site supervisory staff and cleaning personnel prior to contract commencement on April 1, 2027. 10. Staffing and Surge Capacity: Brief narrative explaining the firm�s methodology to recruit, train, and retain qualified custodial labor in the Quantico, VA area in compliance with the Service Contract Labor Standards (41 U.S.C. Chapter 67 / FAR 52.222-41). D. Relevant Past Performance 11. Provide up to three (3) relevant past performance projects completed within the last five (5) years that demonstrate experience similar in size, scope, and complexity to military basewide custodial operations: � Contract Number / Task Order Number (Note: If performed under an IDIQ or BPA, provide specific Task/Delivery Order details, not just the master contract). � Project Title, Facility Type, and Location. � Role (Prime Contractor or Subcontractor; include percentage of work self-performed). � Period of Performance (Award Date and Completion Date). � Total Contract Dollar Value and Approximate Square Footage Maintained. � Brief narrative description of the specific custodial services delivered. � Government or Commercial Point of Contact (Name, Agency/Company, Title, Phone Number, and Email). IV Submission Instructions & Contact Information � Due Date & Time: All responses must be received no later than November 16, 2026, at 2:00 PM EST. Submissions received after this deadline will not be evaluated. � Format: Submissions must be delivered via email in Adobe PDF format. � Email Subject Line: [Contractor Name] Capabilities Statement � Sources Sought N40080-27-R-XXXX � Points of Contact: Primary: Ms. Luz M. Baron, Contract Specialist Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC) Washington / FEAD Quantico Email: luz.m.baron.civ@us.navy.mil Alternate: Ms. Dotty M. Medel, Contracting Officer Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC) Washington / FEAD Quantico Email: dotty.m.medel.civ@us.navy.mil Questions regarding this notice must be submitted in writing via email to the primary point of contact identified above. Thank you for your interest and support of NAVFAC Washington and the Warfighter.

description: ****SOURCES SOUGHT FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY**** This announcement seeks information from industry which will be used for preliminary planning purposes. No proposals are being requested or accepted with this announcement. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS AND NO CONTRACT SHALL BE AWARDED FROM THIS SYNOPSIS. NO SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS OR DRAWINGS ARE AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME. 1. AGENCY: United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Latin America and Caribbean District (SAA) 2. NAICS: 236220 - Commercial and Institutional Building Construction 3. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: Peru 4. ACQUISITION INFORMATION: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Latin America and Caribbean District (SAA), is issuing this Sources Sought announcement as a means of conducting market research to identify parties having an interest in and the resources to support a potential future design-build construction project at the Callao Naval Base, Lima, Peru. The result of this market research will contribute to determining the method of procurement. Estimated Magnitude of Construction: Between $25,000,000 and $50,000,000. Performance Period: 540 days after Notice to Proceed. Anticipated Award Date: Fiscal Year 2027 Quarter 3 Small Business Programs: In accordance with FAR 19.000(b)(1)(ii), the Procuring Contracting Officer (PCO) has elected not to apply FAR Part 19 (Small Business Programs) to this overseas procurement. Consequently, small business set-asides will not be utilized for this project in Peru. However, all responsible sources�including both U.S. concerns (large and small) and foreign entities�are encouraged to submit responses to this Sources Sought notice. 5. ANTICIPATED ACQUISITION STRATEGY: The acquisition strategy for this requirement will be determined based on the responses to this Sources Sought notice and other market research. The Government is considering several compliant acquisition pathways to ensure the successful delivery of this complex Design-Build project in Peru. All interested firms are strongly encouraged to submit a comprehensive capabilities statement, as the information received will be critical in determining the final method of procurement. The primary anticipated strategy is a Two-Phase Design-Build procurement under the authority of FAR Part 36.3. In this scenario, the Government would issue a public Phase 1 solicitation requesting offeror qualifications. Based on these qualifications, the Government would down-select the most highly qualified firms (typically no more than five) who would then be eligible to compete in Phase 2 and submit detailed technical and price proposals. However, based on the unique challenges of performing complex construction in Peru, the Government is also considering the following alternative strategies: Option 1: Limited Competition under FAR Part 6, Other Than Full and Open Competition. If market research reveals that only a very limited number of sources possess the unique combination of Design-Build expertise, mandatory Peruvian licensing (Registro Nacional de Proveedores - RNP), and demonstrated experience with specialized facilities (e.g., POL, medical, secure warehouses) in the local market, the Government may justify limiting competition. Option 2: Establishment of a Qualified Bidders List (QBL) under FAR Part 9.2. If the operational environment in Peru and the specialized nature of the requirement warrant it, the Government may decide to establish a formal Qualification Requirement. Under this authority, the Government would create a list of pre-qualified firms that demonstrate the essential standards for technical capability, financial stability, and in-country operational capacity. Future solicitations for this requirement would then be limited to firms on this established QBL. The Government�s final decision will be based on which strategy provides the best value and ensures a competitive environment among responsible and qualified contractors capable of meeting the demanding technical and logistical requirements of this project. 6. PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The contemplated scope consists of complete Design-Build services�including geotechnical verification, site preparation, civil works, architectural and engineering design after award, structural construction, mechanical/electrical/plumbing (MEP), specialized HVAC/fire suppression, Defense Base Act (DBA) insurance coverage, and Furniture, Fixtures, & Equipment (FF&E). Facility / Scope Package Primary Function Key Technical Considerations Building 110 Spare Parts Warehouse Heavy-duty slab design, industrial racking integration, material handling flow, automated logistics staging. Building 115 Clothing & Gear Warehouse High-density pallet storage, humidity and climate control, inventory distribution bays. Building 112 Material Warehouse Bulk staging, overhead crane/hoist accommodations, heavy equipment ingress/egress ramps. Building 113 Customs Warehouse Secure bonded holding areas, host-nation customs inspection layout, physical security infrastructure. Building 114 Petroleum, Oil, and Lubricants (POL) Warehouse Secondary containment, explosion-proof electrical systems, specialized foam/water fire suppression, environmental drainage controls. Building 111 Medicine & Medical Supplies Warehouse Temperature/humidity-controlled storage (cold chain capability), pharmaceutical-grade clean finishings, backup power integration. Building 120 DIRNOTEMAT & Quality Control Building Administrative offices, testing and quality inspection laboratories, specialized testing benches, IT/telecom infrastructure. Site & Ancillary Works Infrastructure & Integration Site grading, structural fill, perimeter security, access roads, utility connections, complete FF&E packages, and host-nation compliant permitting. 7. SOURCES SOUGHT: The purpose of this source sought is to gain knowledge of interest, capabilities and qualifications of contractors who have the capabilities to complete and perform contracts of this magnitude, and to address any questions, recommendations or concerns from Industry. The Government must ensure there is adequate competition among potential pool of responsible contractors. Prior Government contract work is not required for submitting a response under this Sources Sought announcement. The result of this market research will contribute to determining the method of procurement. 8. RESPONSES: The Capabilities Statement for this Sources Sought is not intended to be a Request for Proposal nor Invitation for Bid, nor does it restrict the Government to an ultimate acquisition approach. It is to request statements regarding the company's ability to demonstrate existing-or-developed expertise and experience in relation to the areas specified herein. Any commercial brochures or currently existing marketing material may also be submitted. This synopsis is for information and planning purposes only and is neither to be construed as a commitment by the Government nor will the Government pay for information solicited. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. Interested parties are requested to provide a capabilities statement addressing the following areas. Section 1: Company Information Company Name, Address, and Website Point of Contact (Name, Title, Phone, Email) CAGE Code and SAM UEI Number Business Size and Status (e.g., Small Business, Large Business) Bonding: What bonding or guarantee methods are available to your company to secure contract performance and protect downstream subcontractor/labor payments for a project located in Peru? Please specify if your company utilizes US Treasury-listed Surety Bonds, Peruvian Bank Letters of Guarantee (Carta Fianza), or Insurance-backed Guarantees (P�liza de Cauci�n). Relevant NAICS Codes Section 2: Interest and Experience in Peru Please confirm your company's interest in performing a design-build construction project of this magnitude and complexity in Lima, Peru. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).

For purposes of this section, Return is defined as physical receipt of the F-condition asset at the contractor?s facility as reflected in the Action Date entry in the Commercial Asset Visibility (CAV) system. In accordance with the CAV Statement of Work, the contractor is required to accurately report all transactions by the end of the fifth regular business day after receipt and the Action Date entered in CAV must be dated to reflect the actual date of physical receipt. The Contractor must obtain final inspection and acceptance by the Government for all assets within the RTATs established in the subsequent contract. Required RTAT: XX days after receipt of asset. Throughput Constraint: Contractor must provide a throughput Constraint for each NSN(s). Total assets to be repaired monthly after initial delivery commences X/month (contractor fill in #). A throughput of 0 per month reflects no throughput constraint. Induction Expiration Date: 365 days after contract award date. Any asset received after this date in days is not authorized for repair without bi-lateral agreement between the Contractor and NAVSUP WSS Contracting Officer. Reconciliation: A reconciliation modification will be issued after final Inspection and acceptance of all assets inducted under the subsequent contract. The parties have agreed to a price (shown on the schedule page) for each unit at the negotiated RTAT. Such prices are based on the Contractor meeting the RTAT requirements described within the schedule page. If the Contractor does not meet the applicable RTAT requirement, consideration will be assessed and subject to negotiation. IF YOU ARE NOT AN APPROVED SOURCE, YOU MUST SUBMIT, TOGETHER WITH YOUR PROPOSAL, THE INFORMATION DETAILED IN THE NAVSUP WSS SOURCE APPROVAL BROCHURE WHICH CAN BE OBTAINED ONLINE AT https://www.navsup.navy.mil/public/navsup/wss/business_opps/ UNDER "COMMODITIES." OFFERS RECEIVED WHICH FAIL TO PROVIDE ALL DATA REQUIRED BY THE SOURCE APPROVAL BROCHURE WILL NOT BE CONSIDERED FOR AWARD UNDER THIS SOLICITATION. PLEASE NOTE, IF EVALUATION OF A SOURCE APPROVAL REQUEST SUBMITTED HEREUNDER CANNOT BE PROCESSED IN TIME AND / OR APPROVAL REQUIREMENTS PRECLUDE THE ABILITY TO OBTAIN SUBJECT ITEMS IN TIME TO MEET GOVERNMENT REQUIREMENTS, AWARD OF REQUIREMENT MAY BE CONTINUED BASED ON FLEET SUPPORT NEEDS. title: Finland – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Kuntotutkimukset
description: Helsingin kaupungin asunnot Oy (Heka) kilpailuttaa konsultit kuntotutkimuksien ja -arvioiden laadintaan. Kohteet, joihin tutkimuksia tilataan, ovat yleensä peruskorjausiässä. Kuntotutkimukset ja -arviot tilataan pääsääntöisesti erilaisten rakennusten korjaushankkeiden suunnittelun lähtötiedoiksi. Lisäksi Heka voi tilata tehtyjen tutkimusten täydennystutkimuksia. Vuosittain osa-aluekohtaiset kuntotutkimustarpeet voivat vaihdella paljon. Kuntotutkimuskokonaisuuden sisältö, laajuus ja tavoitteet määritetään kutakin yksittäistä hanketta varten erikseen. Kuntotutkimuksen tekijältä odotamme vahvaa ammattitaitoa kuntotutkimuksien ja -arvioiden laadinnasta eri aikakausien rakennuksiin, pätevyyttä tehdä tilattavia tutkimuksia ja noudattaa kyseessä olevan tutkimuksen RT- korttia tai muuta virallista ohjeistusta. Hankinta on jaettu kahteentoista osa-alueeseen. Osa-alue 1: Yleinen kuntoarvio Osa-alue 2: Salaojatutkimus Osa-alue 3: Asuinrakennuksen kuntotutkimus Osa-alue 4: Haitta-ainekartoitus Osa-alue 5: Märkätilojen kosteustutkimus Osa-alue 6: Lämmitys-, vesi- ja viemärijärjestelmän tutkimus Osa-alue 7: Ilmanvaihtojärjestelmän tutkimus Osa-alue 8: Radonmittaus Osa-alue 9: Kanava- ja hormitutkimus Osa-alue 10: Sähkö- ja tietojärjestelmätutkimus Osa-alue 11: Lämpökuvaus Osa-alue 12: Tiiviysmittaus Tavallisten vuokra-asuntojen lisäksi Hekalla on liiketiloja ja noin 50 erityisasuntokohdetta (liite erityisasuntokohteet). Lisätietoa kohteista löytyy Hekan verkkosivuilta: https://www.hekaoy.fi/kohteet/tutustu-kohteisiimme/. Hankinta toteutetaan puitejärjestelynä, jossa valitaan enintään kolme konsulttiyritystä per osa-alue. Sopimuskausi on kaksi (2) vuotta ja sopimuksen optiovuoden 1 + 1 vuotta.

title: FY27 Communications and Networking Applied Research Announcement for Office of Naval Research
description: The purpose of this announcement is to focus attention of the scientific community on (1) the area to be studied, and (2) the planned timetable for the submission of white papers and full proposals. The goal of the Communications and Networking Program within the Office of Naval Research (ONR 311) is to support the Navy's Information Warfare vision by developing measurable advances in technology that can directly enable and enhance end-to-end connectivity and quality-of-service for mission-critical information exchange among widely dispersed naval, joint, and coalition forces. The vision is to provide high throughput robust communications and networking to ensure all warfighters � from the operational command to the tactical edge � have access to information, knowledge, and decision-making necessary to perform their assigned tasks. The ONR program is interested in white papers for potential FY27 Applied Research (Budget category 6.2) projects under the following focus areas: Development of long-range VHF-band data link, using compact 4x4 Multiple-Input, Multiple-Output (MIMO) based on 5G/Commercial-Off-The Shelf (COTS) and sub-MHz frequency channelization (spectral efficiency in excess of 1 bit/Hz); Novel design and prototyping of compact electronically-steered apertures for higher frequencies (i.e., above Ka-band); Innovative approaches and technologies for low probability-of-detection communications against advanced electronic threats; Advanced techniques for distributed network control, synchronization, and/or scheduling; and New algorithms for predicting network behavior/performance or emerging operational requirements that are translated into traffic engineering policies. The ONR is receptive to innovative ideas, which are not within the above focus areas, but nonetheless are important to the Navy/Marine Corps communications and networking, as otherwise described in this Topic Description

title: Request for Information: Multi-Source PNT UE
description: Amendment 1: The purpose of this amendment is to change the response date from 16 November 2027 to 16 November 2026. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION MULTI-SOURCE PNT UE 1.0 GENERAL INFORMATION This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for information and planning purposes (market research). This RFI does not constitute a solicitation (Request for Proposal (RFP) or Request for Quotations (RFQ)) or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. This RFI does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. Furthermore, the Government is not, at this time, seeking proposals and will not accept any unsolicited proposals. Respondents are advised the Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the responding party�s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if any is issued. Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly voluntary. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Due to the operational sensitivity of the Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) missions, any future acquisition resulting from this market research will require strict adherence to Department of War (DoW) and Department of Defense (DoD) security, cybersecurity, and supply chain integrity standards. Consequently, while direct responses to this RFI must remain entirely unclassified (reach out to the government contacts below for information on classified submissions), respondents are required to demonstrate their organizational posture regarding facility clearances, information safeguarding, and National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) supply chain compliance. For the purposes of this market research, the anticipated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for manufacturing global positioning systems (GPS) and related equipment is 334220 (Radio and Television Broadcasting and Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing) with a Small Business Size Standard of $44.0 Million, and the primary Product Service Code (PSC) for Global Positioning Systems (GPS) hardware is 5825 (Radio Navigation Equipment, Except Airborne). For specialized, airborne GPS or radar navigation, the code is typically 5826. System-level R&D and engineering services for GPS are usually categorized under codes like R425 (Engineering Services) or AC13 (R&D�Defense System: Electronics). 2.0 BACKGROUND With advances in autonomous systems and guided munitions, the force that can best synchronize its activities at a single point in time and space wields a potent strategic advantage. In the future operating environment, therefore, the Joint Force will increasingly depend on resilient, reliable, and precise position, navigation, and timing (PNT) data to execute combat operations. As such, the Space Force is required to deliver global continuous coverage with stringent civil and military position and timing requirements to assure safety and mission success. This includes at least 88% of the constellation being operationally available more than 98% of the time. Likewise, a thinking adversary will make focused and deliberate efforts to deny access to this capability, leveraging a growing suite of threats including electromagnetic weapons, cyberspace attacks, and kinetic weapons. The challenge today is that, while satellite navigation (SATNAV) through the Global Positioning System (GPS) is foundational to U.S. military operations, critical infrastructure, and global commerce, the current architecture must adapt to evolving jamming and spoofing threats. Additionally, the space and ground segments must be modernized and hardened against physical attack. To build readiness for the future operating environment, therefore, the Space Force will pursue a comprehensive navigation warfare (NAVWAR) strategy that emphasizes resilience, technology modernization, modularity, adaptability, and flexibility. Specifically, it will adopt an open hybrid approach to SATNAV architecture that weighs inputs from diverse sources according to user need, generating a more dependable capability that can withstand adversary action while enabling faster upgrade cycles to enable PNT capabilities. The NAVWAR Objective Force pursues the development and deployment of several key capabilities to advance the SATNAV architecture. One of those elements is User Segment. To make best use of diversified PNT sources, the Space Force will enable a transition to a Multi-Source PNT user equipment (UE) reference architecture that incorporates Modular Open System Architectures (MOSA) and an onboard fusion engine to integrate all available data at the user level. The key enabler of the NAVWAR Objective Force is continued Joint Force investment in Multi-Source PNT UE that utilizes both traditional and new PNT sources. This equipment is foundational to a user�s ability to devise and execute a NAVWAR PACE (i.e., Primary / Alternate / Contingency / Emergency) Plan in degraded or denied environments. While legacy signals are expected to remain supported for civil and public functions, they are increasingly less effective in the contested environment. The military-specific M-Code is available today, while the PNT modernization signals are projected to be available by 2035. 3.0 OBJECTIVE, DESIRED CAPABILITIES AND CHARACTERISTICS This Request for Information (RFI) is focused on obtaining access to analytical information on industrial capabilities in Multi-Source PNT UE the NAVWAR Objective Force. Interests include the following: Multi-Source PNT UE for Terrestrial Users on various military platforms Disadvantaged user High value military assets MOSA Signals supported (M-code, CA, commercial), etc Space Service Volume Multi-Source PNT UE (various orbits) Small satellite users Large satellite users MOSA Signals supported (M-code, CA, commercial), etc Interest is in technical details that can be incorporated into technical analysis to support Space Warfighting Analysis Center, Technology and Emerging Concept Assessments performed during Force Designs. This RFI is being executed in cooperation with the Space Warfighting Analysis Center (SWAC). 4.0 SECURITY, CYBERSECURITY AND SUPPLY CHAIN REQUIREMENTS The secure nature of this requirement dictates adherence to stringent Department of War (DoW) / Department of Defense (DoD) security protocols. While direct responses to this RFI must remain unclassified, respondents shall address their current capabilities and compliance regarding the following security domains: a. Facility and Personnel Security Clearances Given the operational nature of Multi-Source PNT UE and the potential for integration with multiple military architectures, e?orts will likely require access to classified information and systems. Respondents must state their current Facility Clearance Level (FCL) (e.g., None, Secret, Top Secret) and classified safeguarding capabilities. Respondents should confirm their capacity to provide appropriately cleared personnel (Personnel Security Clearances - PCL) and facility infrastructure to support secure development, testing, and operations. Please indicate your facility's current capability and experience in handling, storing, and integrating Communications Security (COMSEC) and Transmission Security (TRANSEC) materials. b. Cybersecurity and Information Safeguarding (CUI/CDI) The protection of Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and Covered Defense Information (CDI) is critical to this effort. In accordance with DFARS 252.204-7012, 7019, and 7020, respondents must describe their current capability to safeguard CUI/CDI. Please indicate your current compliance status with NIST SP 800-171, confirm whether an active assessment score exists within the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS), and state your current readiness posture for the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certi
